classification.difficultyReason: Combine parallel-line and isosceles angle properties to prove similarity, then use matching angles to establish SAS congruence and equal sides.

content.prompt: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram with $\angle BAD$ acute. The point $E$ lies on the ray $CB$ such that $\triangle ABE$ is isosceles with $AB=AE$. The point $F$ lies on the ray $CD$ such that $\triangle ADF$ is isosceles with $AD=AF$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle ABE$ is similar to $\triangle ADF$.

answer.short:
$\triangle ABE\sim\triangle ADF$ (AAA).

Parallel lines and the two isosceles triangles give two matching pairs of equal angles.
answer.worked:
Since $AD\parallel BC$ and $AB\parallel CD$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABE&=\angle BAD &&\text{(alternate angles)}\\\angle ADF&=\angle BAD &&\text{(alternate angles)}.\end{align*}$$
Also,
$$\begin{align*}\angle AEB&=\angle ABE &&\text{(base angles, }AB=AE\text{)}\\\angle AFD&=\angle ADF &&\text{(base angles, }AD=AF\text{)}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\angle ABE=\angle ADF$ and $\angle AEB=\angle AFD$, so $\triangle ABE\sim\triangle ADF$ (AAA).

answer.short:
$DE=BF$.

$\triangle ABF\cong\triangle AED$ by SAS, using the equal apex angles from part a.
answer.worked:
From part a, $\angle BAE=\angle DAF$ (matching angles of similar triangles). By addition of adjacent angles,
$$\begin{align*}\angle EAD&=\angle EAB+\angle BAD\\\angle FAB&=\angle DAF+\angle BAD.\end{align*}$$
Hence $\angle EAD=\angle FAB$.

In $\triangle ABF$ and $\triangle AED$,
$$\begin{align*}AB&=AE &&\text{(given)}\\AF&=AD &&\text{(given)}\\\angle BAF&=\angle EAD.\end{align*}$$
Thus $\triangle ABF\cong\triangle AED$ (SAS), so $DE=BF$ (matching sides of congruent triangles).
